data.one_liner: Synchronizes scroll positions of multiple scrollable widgets.
data.what_it_does: Provides a controller group that keeps several ScrollControllers in sync. When one scrolls, all others jump to the same offset. It supports dynamic addition of controllers and offers animateTo/jumpTo for the group.
use_when: You need two or more scrollable widgets to move together, e.g., side‑by‑side lists or horizontally scrolling items inside a vertical list.
You want a simple, null‑safe solution without external dependencies or code generation.
You are building a Flutter app that targets Android, iOS, web, macOS, Windows, or Linux.
You prefer an imperative API that works directly with ScrollControllers.
avoid_when: You need complex scrolling behavior like parallax or nested scroll physics that require custom scroll physics.
You are already using a state‑management solution that handles scroll positions differently and you want to avoid duplicate controllers.
strengths: Supports dynamic controller addition with unique keys.
Provides group animateTo/jumpTo for coordinated scrolling.
weaknesses: Only synchronizes scroll offset, no advanced physics or animations.
Requires unique keys when adding controllers dynamically to avoid offset drift.
Limited to scrollable widgets; not a general state‑management tool.
